task.description:
WF-01, step 1 — write requirements for automated end-to-end (e2e) tests of the Sai web pages in a REAL headless Chrome.

OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-11-03, Claude Code session in VS Code, message to ORCH): «по проекту sai  используй инструкции [другого проекта владельца] и sai. Чтобы убрать ошибки и покрыть тестами проект, а именно e2e тесты». Put these words into original_request of every requirement you write.

FACTS CHECKED BY ORCH ON 2026-11-03 (verify the ones you rely on yourself, quality-bar Q3):
1. Baseline at HEAD f806d7d on the Mac, Node 22.23.4: format:check, lint, traces (2372 files, 0 traces) and handoffs-check (1280 files, 0 violations) are green; `npm test` is 2135 of 2135 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, about 233 s. So there is no red test to fix; the gap is the lack of e2e.
2. The automated suite has NO real-browser test: the pages are tested against hand-made DOM stubs (tools/test/picker-page-dom.js, tools/test/team-web-dom.js and similar). A real headless Chrome is used only by UAT-RUNNER agents by hand at acceptance (.claude/agents/uat-runner.md, items 5 and following) and leaves no repeatable test behind.
3. Three web surfaces exist and are the scope: Pixel Office (tools/src/pixel-office/, start `npm run pixel-office -- --port 0`), the solution picker site (tools/src/picker/, start `npm run picker -- serve --tenants <folder> --port 0`, demo tenants in tools/src/picker/demo-tenants-v3/) and the team web page (tools/src/web/, start `npm run team-web`). Read their README sections and requirements for exact start keys and behaviour.
4. Feasibility sketch ORCH ran outside the project: Node 22 alone (child_process + global WebSocket + fetch to the Chrome debugging port) starts `Google Chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=<temp>`, opens a local page, clicks a button and reads the changed title; no npm dependency is needed. A window narrower than about 500 px needs `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`. Chrome is installed on the Mac at /Applications/Google Chrome.app; the CI runner (.github/workflows/check.yml) is ubuntu-24.04 with Node 22 — whether Chrome is available there must be CHECKED by a criterion or stated as an open question for the owner, not assumed.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Node 22 without run-time dependencies (decisions/0002, 0015); no new npm package, not even a dev one, without a decision record — prefer none.
- quality-bar Q4 (one check command `cd tools && npm run check`), Q5 (a test per criterion), Q6 (no skip, no `|| true`; if Chrome is missing the e2e must FAIL with an understandable message, not skip), Q10 (a failing external thing gives a clear message), R2 (tests must never write into the owner's real Pixel Office journal: use a temporary SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR and a free port), Q7 (no secrets).
- Tests must be independent of each other and of the clock/order; pages and servers started on port 0 on 127.0.0.1; every temp folder and every Chrome process cleaned up even on failure; screenshots and Chrome profiles go outside the project.
- Total added time must stay inside the 30-minute limit of check.yml (decisions/0106); say in a criterion how it is measured.
- Do not write the name of any other project or of any person's product into Sai files (decisions/0082). Practices taken from an outside reference, written neutrally: keep the slow browser suite as its own command also runnable alone; record in the run output the command, the selection, the exit code and the duration; a baseline of screenshots/DOM snapshots is compared by structure and meaning, not by pixels (as in DESIGN-QA-VALIDATOR).

WHAT TO WRITE: two to four requirements (WF-01 step 1, item 5: one piece of work for one run each, linked by depends_on). Suggested split, change it if you can justify it:
 (A) an e2e kit in tools/test: a Chrome launcher and a debugging-protocol client in pure Node, viewport and theme/language switching, console-error collection, cleanup, a Chrome-missing message — with its own tests (including a fault test: Chrome binary not found, Chrome killed mid-test); and a separate command `npm run e2e` that is also part of `npm run check`;
 (B) e2e of the picker site: a visitor opens a demo tenant in each of ru/kk/en, answers the questionnaire, sees the result; light and dark theme; windows 1470×784, 390×844, 320×568 without horizontal scroll; a second tenant does not show the first tenant's data (Q8); a bad address/tenant gives the understandable page, not a crash;
 (C) e2e of Pixel Office: with a temporary state folder and a free port, a hook event posted to the server shows on the page within 5 seconds without reload (the claim of REQ-001), the journal row has the right words, the owner's real folder is untouched (R2), a secret in an event text appears masked on the page;
 (D) e2e of the team web page: create a project, see it in the list, open it, pause/resume if the page offers it, the chat message appears; failures of the engine give a human message (Q10); with a scripted (fake) executor only — NO real Claude session and no spending.
Each criterion must say what checks it (a command or a named test file; the named test file is "created by this work"), and have a "before" value that is NOT satisfied on HEAD (AP-071): for example `grep` finds no file using the debugging port in tools/test now.

Look for guard tests in tools/test that a new folder, new npm script or changed `check` script would turn red (AP-068/112/113) and name the replacement table in the description of the requirement that causes it. Next free REQ number: the largest in the whole file plus one (REQ-103 exists, check for more).

EDIT SCOPE: only new blocks at the END of docs/requirements.yaml; nothing else in the repository is changed. Take the hash of the rest of the file before and after (WF-01 step 1, item 7) and write the "before copy" from the tag base/E2E-20261103-01.

Questions you cannot decide go into result.issues (do not guess): in particular (1) whether e2e belongs inside `npm run check` given the 30-minute limit and the Chrome availability on the CI runner; (2) the Chrome binary lookup (env variable SAI_CHROME, standard Mac and Linux paths); (3) anything in the three pages that cannot be driven without a real Claude session.
acceptance_criteria: At least two criteria per requirement, each with a named way of checking
Rest of docs/requirements.yaml unchanged (hash before and after in result)
No name of another project in the text

issues.text: The task of this handoff (line 28, the owner's verbatim words) contains the name of the owner's other project, which the traces check treats as a forbidden name (decisions/0082); `cd tools && npm run traces` now exits 1 with one trace, so the instructed run of traces cannot be green and `npm run check` is red in this tree until the line is fixed. The exceptions file does not apply to names. I cannot edit `task`. In the requirements the name is replaced by the placeholder [другого проекта владельца] and the text says so, as REQ-033 does with its [образец]. Proposal for ORCH: replace the name by a placeholder in the handoff by an orch_correction or rewrite the task line before the gate, and check that REQ-VALIDATOR accepts the placeholder as 'verbatim' (item е).

Question 1 of the task - does e2e belong inside `npm run check`? Proposal: yes. decisions/0023 D2 already says browser tests are inside `check` with no exceptions (a separate-only command was rejected there as a Q4 violation), so REQ-104 adds a separate command that is also the last step of `check`. Open risks, settled by criteria 8-10 of REQ-104 and not assumed: (a) Chrome on the ubuntu-24.04 runner is not verified (I did not check it); (b) Chrome may need to start without its sandbox there (unprivileged user namespaces are restricted on that image) - starting without the sandbox is a security decision, the kit opens only 127.0.0.1 pages of Sai (criterion 5) but it still needs an owner's record; (c) time: the suite takes about 235 s on this Mac and the earlier GitHub runs took 10-14.7 min, the first run with REQ-102 hit the old 15-minute limit; the e2e budget is 240 s in total and the 25-minute watch value of decisions/0106 is the stop; (d) the pre-push hook runs `npm run check`, so every push will need Chrome (its text 'about 2 minutes' and the README guard 'about 2 minutes' are already out of date and are not touched). Proposal for a record in decisions/ (Q12): 0107 - real-Chrome e2e inside `check`, spec files `*.e2e.js` outside the glob of `test`, no browser dependency, what happens if the runner has no Chrome or needs --no-sandbox.

Question 2 - the Chrome lookup. Proposed in REQ-104 and open for confirmation: the variable SAI_CHROME first (a wrong value fails and does not fall back), then the standard macOS place, then google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, chromium-browser from PATH. Windows places are left out because the full check was never run on Windows; SAI_CHROME works there. The language of the Chrome-missing message is left to the design (the criteria check the content: the variable name and every place tried, no stack).

Question 3 - what cannot be driven without a real Claude session. Pixel Office: nothing in REQ-106 needs one - events go through the real hook program with composed payloads into a throwaway folder; this does NOT replace the real-session acceptance of REQ-001 (criterion 1 and the UAT items, blocked by decisions/0099), and REQ-106 does not list REQ-001 in depends_on for that reason. Team page: only the scripted executor is driven (README: for tests only); real claude-cli runs, real spending, and answering a task's question (not on the page yet, README) are not covered; a trap program proves no real run starts. Picker: the screen after 'Показать результат' is a placeholder (result.js), so the spec checks its structure and the server's answer, not its words; the future result-screen requirements (REQ-071 and later) must replace those assertions in their own tables.

REQ-033 (pending, 'tests of the team page in jsdom', devDependency, decisions/0022 D7 and 0023 D2) overlaps REQ-107 and promises 'no separate command'; its jsdom would be the first development dependency added since decisions/0002 and would not see layout, themes or scrolling. I did not touch it. Proposal for ORCH and the owner: a record in decisions/ that the real-Chrome e2e of REQ-104..107 takes the place of REQ-033 (cancel or narrow REQ-033, no jsdom). 0022 D7 already says the owner may demand a real browser.

Size (AP-016): REQ-104 is the biggest (12 criteria: kit, fault tests, command, check wiring, six replaced guard tests, README). I kept it as one job because the command is useless without the kit and the table has to be done once. If REQ-VALIDATOR returns (г), the natural split is REQ-104a criteria 1-6 (kit) and REQ-104b criteria 7-12 (command, wiring, time, CI, clean tree, README).

Real defects may be found by the new specs (contrast of 4.5 on the picker text in both themes, overflow at 320 px in Kazakh, a visible focus outline on every control, the Pixel Office and team page in narrow windows). No requirement promised some of these before, so I put into the criteria only what a README or an earlier requirement says or what WCAG fixes; a found defect goes by WF-03 (stated in REQ-105..107), the criterion is not weakened. Horizontal overflow of Pixel Office and the team page at 390 and 320 px is deliberately not asserted - an owner's question whether it should be a requirement.

Test-data note (R2): REQ-106 sends composed payloads through the real hook program into a throwaway state folder under the temporary root with HOME redirected; the starter refuses any other folder (criterion 1) and criterion 5 compares the owner's real journal before and after. I judged this inside R2 (the same rule UAT-RUNNER works by); SECURITY-REVIEWER should confirm.
